acceptance_criteria.description: Successful owned-process cleanup transitions the same durable lease instance active-to-closing-to-closed and removes it without an invalid stale-state transition.
Retryable and failed postcondition paths transition from the current persisted lease state, retain the lease, and preserve all fail-closed ownership checks.
Focused SessionManager tests prove successful convergence and retryable counterexamples with durable lease state validation.
The clean real Tinto stdio probe reaches READY, returns bounded observation evidence, succeeds on the first close with state idle, and leaves no new current-run durable lease.

closed_decisions: The clean real-Tinto stdio probe reaches READY and produces bounded observation evidence.
Recursive close diagnostics prove the sole first-close failure is Invalid custody lease transition active -> closed.
SessionManager stores the result of active-to-closing in this.#durableLease but keeps using the stale local active lease for closed/retryable transitions.
The fix must carry the persisted current lease value through all later transitions in the same cleanup attempt.
Do not change custody termination, ownership proof, public MCP behavior, provider protocol, environment reconstruction, or crash-recovery policy.
forbidden_changes: Do not edit files outside the two owned files.
Do not weaken identity, nonce, custody, descendant, listener, or durable transition validation.
Do not add transition bypasses, force removal, unbounded waits, broader termination, or fallback deletion.
Do not change public MCP tools/schemas/dialog behavior, provider/Tinto source, dependencies, manifests, lockfiles, queue/blocker/release files, commits, branches, Jira, or pull requests.
objective: Fix the proven durable-custody lease state bug where successful application cleanup persists active-to-closing but later reuses the stale active lease for the closing-to-closed transition, causing the first close to fail while a retry succeeds.
